candidates.title: Both sides of Alberta separation debate rally as momentum kicks up ahead of vote
candidates.description: Summer is winding down — and Alberta's separation debate is ramping up, as both sides laid the path ahead for their respective movements with rallies on Saturday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Google updates maps to display Lake Ontario as Lake America in U.S.
candidates.description: Google Maps has updated to display "Lake America" when people in the United States search for the name.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Sask. woman crowned Mrs. Canada Universe after 26 years away from the stage
candidates.description: Jasmin Esquivel of Prince Albert, Sask., won the national pageant in Surrey, B.C. and will represent Canada at the Mrs. Universe 2026 competition in Sri Lanka this fall. She says her children are her greatest support.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tenants in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside are working to make their buildings safer during heat waves
candidates.description: A group of tenants in Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside is demonstrating how communities can come together to keep each other safe during extreme heat events.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ford responds to Trump's renaming effort with Lake Ontario 'Now and Always' sign
candidates.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a Lake Ontario sign in Hamilton on Saturday, after U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order to change the name to "Lake America" amid deteriorating relations.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What are the rules about AI ads in municipal campaigns?
candidates.description: Across Ontario, candidates are being certified to run for municipal offices in October, and experts tell CBC there are no rules regulating how they use artificial intelligence to advertise.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Days after deadly Nepal flood, families of missing B.C. couples desperate for details
candidates.description: Days after a massive wall of water tore through the Timure region of Nepal, families of two missing Metro Vancouver couples are desperately searching for information about their loved ones.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why this northern B.C. community is giving out 23-year-old toilets for free
candidates.description: The District of Port Edwards is giving away free low-flush toilets that have been sitting unused in the district office basement for the past two decades.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Toronto cinema says it was forced to cancel screenings over decades-old, unofficial 'zone' system
candidates.description: A downtown Toronto cinema says it was forced to cancel screenings of a new movie after the film’s distributor unexpectedly withdrew access — citing a decades-old practice in Canada that limits which theatres can show movies first.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Winnipeg's 1st female mayor wants to see a 2nd. That's not likely in this fall's election
candidates.description: Susan Thompson is the first — and only — woman to serve as Winnipeg's mayor. Nearly three decades after she left office, she says it's taking too long for a second woman to be sworn in.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nova Scotia father and son haul hooked bald eagle out of lake, safely free it on shore
candidates.description: Bryan Esbaugh and his 15-year-old son, Wyatt, were fishing on Ponhook Lake in Queens County, N.S., when they accidentally hooked a bald eagle. After safely untangling the bird on shore, they set it free and playfully dubbed it the "Canadian White-Headed Lake Raptor."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Eastlink says data breach affects 75,000 customers
candidates.description: Telecommunications provider Eastlink is warning some customers of a potential data breach that happened in recent days, but it does not believe that credit card or banking information was exposed. The company operates in seven Canadian provinces and Bermuda.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Kawacatoose First Nation celebrates return of teepee cover stolen over a century ago in emotional ceremony
candidates.description: It was an emotional afternoon at Kawacatoose First Nation Friday. After a century-long absence, a stolen teepee cover has now been returned to its rightful owners.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'We didn’t want them:' Hamilton rallies against Dominion Society, as group holds event in Burlington, Ont.
candidates.description: More than 100 people gathered outside of Hamilton city hall around midday Saturday to denounce the fact that a self-proclaimed nationalist group that wants to deport millions of people from Canada planned to host a day-long conference in the city the same day. Dominion Society members were seen meeting in Burlington, Ont.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: An island mysteriously appeared — then disappeared — on B.C.'s largest reservoir
candidates.description: B.C. Hydro says it's monitoring for the reappearance of a mysterious island first spotted by boaters 100 kilometres from the W.A.C. Bennett Dam in northeastern B.C.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Buck Martinez inducted into Blue Jays' new Hall of Excellence at Rogers Centre
candidates.description: John Albert (Buck) Martinez, a cancer survivor, catcher, manager and broadcaster for parts of five decades with the Toronto Blue Jays, was inducted into the club's new Hall of Excellence on Saturday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's Sophia Jensen wins gold at canoe sprint world championships in Poland
candidates.description: Canada's Sophia Jensen won the first world title of her career on Saturday at the 2026 ICF Canoe Sprint & Paracanoe World Championships in Poznań, Poland.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa couple's 'Lake Ontario' hats selling like hotcakes after Trump's executive order
candidates.description: Before the ink had even dried on U.S. President Donald Trump's executive order to rename Lake Ontario, a Canadian company was already selling hats with the Great Lake's true name emblazoned on it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's Danielle Dorris swims to silver in women's butterfly S5-7 at Para Pan Pacific Championships
candidates.description: Two-time Paralympic champion Danielle Dorris of Moncton, N.B., earned Canada's first medal to open the three-day Pan Pacific Swimming Championships, grabbing silver in the women's 50-metre butterfly S5-7 final on Friday night in Walnut, Calif.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: As Germany's far right gains ground, coded symbols are hiding in plain sight
candidates.description: As Germany’s far right gains political ground, researchers say some of its supporters are becoming more comfortable signalling their views in public — sometimes without displaying an explicitly political symbol at all.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: At least 7 dead after ferry carrying nearly 270 passengers, crew capsizes off northern Cyprus
candidates.description: Some 237 people have been rescued, Northern Cyprus Prime Minister Unal Ustel told Turkish state-run TRT news channel. He said a search was underway for another 24 people.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nepal warns of possible fresh flooding as communities grapple with devastation
candidates.description: Authorities in Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding on Sunday and urged residents in flood-affected districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 3-year-old boy among 2 Palestinians killed by Israeli strike, Gaza medics say
candidates.description: An Israeli airstrike killed two Palestinians, including a three-year-old child, in the central Gaza Strip on Sunday, health officials said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Icelanders vote to stay out of EU in close-fought referendum
candidates.description: Icelanders voted to stay out of the European Union, referendum results showed on Sunday, as they rejected a government push to reopen membership talks and sided with those who said Iceland's fishing waters were too important to risk.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Shooting at rave in Switzerland kills 1 and injures 5
candidates.description: A 22-year-old woman died of injuries at the scene. Four men and one woman, between 24 and 27 years old, were taken to the hospital with injuries ranging from minor to severe.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: In Ohio, Canada-U.S. trade war sparks anger and uncertainty
candidates.description: Youngstown, Ohio, sits in a wider congressional district known as OH-6, which exports more than $820 million US in goods to Canada every year. While not all of its imports and exports are caught in the crosshairs of the escalating U.S-Canadian tariffs, a prolonged trade war could threaten some businesses in those sectors.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump's Venezuelan oil deal: What we know and how it could impact Canada's oil industry
candidates.description: Several questions about the U.S. deal to develop vast Venezuelan oil reserves remain unanswered, and a rapid and large-scale increase in production is unlikely. But experts say increased exports from Venezuela "would compete directly with Canadian crude in the U.S. Gulf Coast market."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: As insults fly around trade, negotiators for Canada and the U.S. avoid getting personal in public
candidates.description: Politicians from Canada and the U.S. have thrown varying degrees of personal insults back and forth across the border this week, but the two governments' trade negotiators avoided getting personal — at least in public. Experts believe the two trade leads are striking a different tone because they have a different role to play as the dispute heats up.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump administration video showing Haitian deportees in chains sparks outrage
candidates.description: A U.S. Department of Homeland Security video shows men, handcuffed and in chains, boarding a deportation flight to Haiti this week. Critics say the Trump administration is "bragging" about sending Haitian immigrants "back to a war-torn country" after rescinding temporary protected status.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli settlers attack home in occupied West Bank's Qusra: witnesses
candidates.description: Dozens of masked Israeli settler militants attacked homes surrounding the occupied West Bank village of Qusra on Saturday, the first major attack since a siege by settlers in the area earlier this month drew an international outcry. The settlers surrounded a Palestinian home, throwing stones while seven Palestinians were trapped inside, according to witnesses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russian attack on Kyiv region kills at least 38
candidates.description: The death toll from a Russian strike on a warehouse west of Kyiv, the war's deadliest attack so far this year, rose to 38 with four people still missing, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on social media Sunday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Will Bessent's bond market intervention make U.S. inflation worse? | About That
candidates.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's recent intervention in the bond market is setting off alarm bells for many investors and analysts. Avneet Dhillon breaks down concerns that Bessent’s attempt to calm the markets and decrease the cost of borrowing may actually worsen inflation. (Photo credits: The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images)
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iceland votes on whether to start EU membership talks in shadow of Trump's Greenland threats
candidates.description: About 265,000 Icelanders are eligible to vote in a referendum on whether to trigger European Union membership talks. Supporters say membership could offer stability and protection against possible threats from U.S. President Donald Trump, while opponents say it's unnecessary and could endanger rich fishing stocks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says U.S. makes deal to control 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday that his administration has entered a sweeping agreement with Venezuela that, if realized, could give the U.S. access to vast amounts of the South American country's untapped oil reserves, at cost.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Old soup factory takes on new high-tech life as quantum computing firm gets $195M federal boost
candidates.description: In the echoey void of a gutted Campbell's Soup factory in Toronto’s west end, Canada's minister of artificial intelligence and digital innovation announced the federal government’s biggest bet to date on homegrown technology that could revolutionize artificial intelligence, medical science and a host of other key sectors of the economy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's economy has found its footing. But is it enough to survive the U.S. trade war?
candidates.description: GDP growth surged in the spring. Exports, business investment and household spending showed how Canada can weather the trade war storm. The question is whether it can last.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Eight killed and others missing after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus
candidates.description: A search and rescue operation is under way after a ferry carrying nearly 270 people turns over after leaving port.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Nasa launches new space telescope able to see 100 times more than Hubble
candidates.description: The US space agency's telescope is starting a multi-year mission to create a new map of the universe and learn more about dark energy and dark matter.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Canada installs large Lake Ontario sign in latest jab at US
candidates.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a billboard on Canada's shoreline with the message: "Lake Ontario. Now and Always."
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Norway's new king remembers 'my dear father' in first speech
candidates.description: Haakon VIII pays emotional tribute to his late father, Harald V, before outlining how he wishes to reign.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Former Ecuadorian president imprisoned for corruption
candidates.description: Lenín Moreno denies taking bribes from a Chinese firm to secure a contract to build a hydroelectric plant.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator ordered to pay $172,000 for Trump speech bets
candidates.description: The staffer was found to have used his prior knowledge of the president's speeches to place lucrative bets.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Berlin is being blackmailed by hackers, mayor says
candidates.description: Kai Wegner says the German capital and city-state would not cave in to a ransom demand for data stolen in a cyber-attack.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: They fell in love - then had to check they weren't brother and sister
candidates.description: A French couple - both conceived by sperm donors - wanted children. But with home DNA tests illegal, how could they be sure they were not related?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: WhatsApp chat used to launder cash for crime and extremism
candidates.description: The WhatsApp money launderers arranged cash transfers in the UK and around the world with no paper trail.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Australia usually hosts the world's biggest cuttlefish mating event - not this year
candidates.description: According to official figures only 1,811 cuttlefish turned up to mate this year, down 97% on last year.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Somali piracy surges as the impact of the US-Iran war ripples outwards
candidates.description: Two ships were seized within four days last week raising to at least 13 the number attacked since January.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Footage of Tibet floods isn't being shown in China - and we know little about victims there
candidates.description: Some of the most dramatic footage from the deadly flash flooding is hidden from public view in China.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What tariffs will really cost Canadians and Americans
candidates.description: Households and businesses have become used to tariffs impacting the cost of living for more than year now, so what will change now?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Deadly strike on Kyiv warehouse prompts evacuations
candidates.description: Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson reports from Kyiv after the deadly strike, which authorities said killed more than 30 people.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: I've been to Gamescom six times - here's what excited me this year
candidates.description: The BBC's Laura Cress gets a first look at the biggest games in Cologne from Witcher 3 to Alien: Isolation 2.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'A giant leap forward': Nasa launches powerful new space telescope to explore mysteries of the Universe
candidates.description: The US space agency's telescope is starting a multi-year mission to create a new map of the universe and learn more about dark energy and dark matter.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Thunderstorms and gusty winds set to continue into Bank Holiday Monday
candidates.description: Cooler and showery conditions will continue across the weekend and into Monday, bringing a record-breaking summer to a rather damp close as Matt Taylor explains.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How the weather in space can affect us on Earth - and the team trying to protect us
candidates.description: The weather in space has the potential to impact our lives here on Earth in a fundamental way.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Canada claps back at Trump's efforts to rename Lake Ontario as 'Lake America'
candidates.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford has unveiled a giant billboard reading: "Lake Ontario — Now and Always." But tech giant Google has said it is renaming the lake for U.S. users, as President Trump demanded.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Energy experts have doubts about Trump's newly proposed Venezuelan oil deal
candidates.description: There are many reasons to be skeptical of the Trump administration's announcement that the U.S. will develop Venezuelan oil.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: From Appalachia to Africa: Why Dolly Parton was beloved across the continent
candidates.description: Dolly Parton's songs traveled far beyond Nashville. Across Africa, musicians embraced her stories of hardship, heartbreak and humble beginnings — and made them their own.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Nepal warns of possible fresh flooding as communities grapple with devastation
candidates.description: Authorities in Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding on Sunday and urged residents in flood-affected districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Icelanders vote 'no' to talks aimed at joining the EU in close referendum
candidates.description: The vote against the EU led by 52.8 percent with nearly all votes counted, according to RÚV , Iceland's broadcaster.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Getting help to Nepal's flood survivors is proving difficult
candidates.description: Blocked roads and monsoon weather are complicating efforts to get food, shelter and emergency hygeine to survivors of Nepal's catastrophic floods. World Vision's Dhruba Gurmachhan explains what survivors need the most.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Rescuers race to find thousands missing after deadly Himalayan floods
candidates.description: Rescue crews are struggling through blocked roads, high mountain canyons and dangerous terrain as they search for thousands of people missing in Nepal and Tibet.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Russian strike near Kyiv kills 37, in one of the year's deadliest attacks
candidates.description: The deadly strike comes amid 72 hours of near constant drone strikes across Ukraine, severely disrupting daily life.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Photos: See the aftermath of deadly flash floods in Nepal
candidates.description: Nepal officials say the death toll has continues to rise in Wednesday's floods that washed away communities in Nepal and Tibet, which is held by China. About 2,500 people are missing in both areas.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Srebrenica survivor Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death
candidates.description: Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death with NPR's Scott Simon. All of Hrustanovic's adult male relatives died in the Srebrenica Massacre engineered by Mladic.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How a comic book store got swept into the tariff storm
candidates.description: Tariffs continue to rile all kinds of American businesses more than a year after Trump unveiled his first set of tariffs — including a comic book store owner in Ohio.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Social media restrictions on young users: What do the kids say?
candidates.description: We've heard from adults about the new Facebook and Instagram rules, but what are kids saying? Teenage social media users talk about whether the proposed restrictions will have any effect on them.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Medicare's pilot GLP-1 discount program has a catch. Some sick patients don't qualify
candidates.description: Medicare launched a pilot program that could streamline the process to get GLP-1s, with some seniors paying just $50 a month. But many people with the most serious illnesses won't get that discount.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The bridges of Rwanda open up new worlds
candidates.description: A charity built 96 bridges to connect communities separated by rivers and gorges. A new study looks at the life-changing impact of a concrete-and-steel pedestrian crossing.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pennsylvania measles deaths ignite clash over RFK Jr.'s vaccination claims
candidates.description: Two deaths associated with the measles outbreak in Pennsylvania prompted messaging from the health secretary that both encouraged and undermined vaccinations.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Lights out, Instagram off? The changes to Meta for teens could be a big deal
candidates.description: Researchers and advocates are applauding the changes that Meta agreed to make for minors on Instagram and Facebook. Cutting kids off at night and during the school day are two big changes.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. relied on these science advisers. Then the Trump administration cut them
candidates.description: The federal government recruits top experts to volunteer to advise on pressing research issues of the day. Since President Trump took office, hundreds of these experts have been dismissed.
candidates.author: NPR
